Yeah, I think it's being over used. Bombs exploding, gunman shooting, buildings being burned down and more being done to terrify, frighten and intimidate targets, is what I think terrorism really is about. It is violent and it is meant to send a message and threat. However, terrorism is being used a bit too easily in my opinion. #OregonUnderAttack isn't terrorism. BLM or Occupy Wallstreet isn't terrorism. They are both protests (though some are more violent than others, but I won't get into that).

The Boston Marathon Bombing was terrorism, the San Bernardino shooting was terrorism. People died and a message was sent: "You aren't safe". These weren't incidents that stemmed from protests or disgruntled employees, it came from an ideology that meant to harm. People throw terrorism very loosely nowadays. If we were to use the dictionary definition, sure we can interpret it very loosely.

Terrorism

The unlawful use or threatened use of force or violence by a person or an organized group against people or property with the intention of intimidating or coercing societies or governments, often for ideological or political reasons.

BLM could be considered domestic terrorists, because they've been known to hurt people. They have an ideology that they want to enforce and their targets is society and more specifically institutions owned by the governments (Police, schools and cities). They've done more damage than the Oregon occupation, who have only taken over an empty building.

Terrorism is more the connotation instead of the denotation. The fear, the terror, the fear, not the requirements.

Terrorism has always just been a label used by groups calling themselves governments to differentiate their own violence from those of other political entities they don't recognize.

ISIS calling themselves a state seems highly appropriate to me, they are just a bunch of violent thugs trying to coerce people to obey their mandates like any other. That's not to say I support them; quite the contrary. I just don't see other claimed states to be that much better from a moralistic perspective.
My definition of a terrorist and who rightfully deserves it hasn't been influenced by outside interference, and as such hasn't changed or lost meaning.
No, people are just using it wrong.

A profound feeling of emptiness rushes through the first Golem. This is new. Feelings are slow, cautious things, creeping and inching through. But this, this... void. Afted the first rushing, stinging loss, new, unwelcome emotions steal out to claim him. Numbing, chilly feelings, the final disconnect from the Creator. This has only one solution. They must strive to become those that Tempest would want to give His grace to. They must toil and become greater. They will redouble their efforts to grow and learn, and the first step is to make more Golem.

But the ache of this new void still chills him to his core.
